title: Month-End Close: Airport CFO Review
description: The board wants the ledger story, not noise. Answer the close questions and defend the airport's numbers.

questions.prompt: Cash increased, but revenue did not increase by the same amount. What is the most likely explanation?
choices: Some cash movement may relate to collections, financing, deferred revenue, or working capital - not all cash is revenue.
Cash and revenue should always move by the same amount.
The airport should record all cash receipts as concessions revenue.
Revenue only changes when debt is repaid.

questions.prompt: Why does stretching Accounts Payable improve short-term cash but increase risk?
choices: It delays cash outflow but can damage vendor terms, service reliability, and audit/compliance posture.
It permanently reduces the amount owed to vendors.
It turns every unpaid bill into equity.
It increases passenger facility charges automatically.

questions.prompt: Passenger facility charges are collected with passenger activity. What should the CFO verify at month close?
choices: That collected/earned amounts are properly recognized and any deferred or restricted amounts are not treated as free operating cash.
That all passenger-related cash is posted to payroll expense.
That passenger facility charges are excluded from the ledger.
That collected amounts are always unrestricted profit.

questions.prompt: Why does interest expense reduce earnings even when principal repayment is separate?
choices: Interest is the cost of borrowing and hits the income statement; principal repayment changes the balance sheet and financing cash flow.
Interest is an asset, while principal is revenue.
Principal repayment is the only borrowing cost shown on the income statement.
Interest expense should be ignored when cash is tight.
